source.notes: No official marking scheme is published with this paper; questions carry no official answer. Genuine ICSE 2024 board examination paper from the official CISCE Archive Library ZIP bundle; paper code printed on every page: 'T24 501'. 8 printed pages. Structure: Part I (30 marks, compulsory) = Question 1 (sixteen 1-mark MCQs, (i)-(xvi); the [16] bracket covers the whole question, so each item is recorded as 1 mark from the instructions) + Question 2 (seven 2-mark short answers). Part II: Section A (Questions 3-5, attempt any two, 10 marks each) and Section B (Questions 6-10, attempt any three, 10 marks each). All Part II questions are included, so the marks in this file add up to 110 (30 + 30 + 50), not the printed maximum of 80; that is expected for a pick-2-of-3 / pick-3-of-5 paper. The introductory stem of each Part II question is omitted from its sub-parts unless a sub-part depends on it (picture/passage). On pages 3-4 the sub-part labels (vi)-(xv) are printed in a separate column; they were assigned to the questions in printed order. Pictures/cartoon for Question 1 (iii), 1 (xvi) and Question 8 are not reproduced; the Question 1 (iv) table is rebuilt as text rows. Question 8 is kept as one 10-mark entry because (ii) depends on (i). The Question 9 passage (The Guardian editorial, 12 January 1920) is repeated in each of its sub-parts.
source.usage: Official CISCE board examination paper from the CISCE Archive Library (cisce.org/archive-library); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text: Mention any two writs issued by the High Court.
Imagine you are an Indian ruler who has signed the Subsidiary Alliance. Mention any two conditions of this agreement which will affect you.
Mention any two causes of the Quit India Movement.
In which year did the Surat Split happen? What was the result of this split?
Mention any two common ideologies of Fascism and Nazism.
Name the two cities of Japan which were bombed by America in the year 1945.

Read the given news carefully and answer the question that follows:
Govt’s power to promulgate, repromulgate Ordinances — why and how
An Ordinance “shall have the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament”. But the government is required to bring an Ordinance before Parliament for ratification — and failure to do so will lead to its lapsing “at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament”.
The Indian Express – May 25, 2023
Mention any two points regarding an ordinance that can be deduced from the above news.
The Rajya Sabha is called a Permanent House. Explain this statement.
Explain the composition of the Rajya Sabha.
Mention any two exclusive powers of the Lok Sabha and two powers exclusive to the Rajya Sabha.
Mention any three points to distinguish between the Council of Ministers and the Cabinet.
Who appoints the Cabinet Ministers? Mention any two administrative powers of the Cabinet.
The President is the nominal head of the Indian Union. Mention any four functions of the Prime Minister with reference to the President.
What is the composition of the Supreme Court? Why is it called the Court of Record?
Explain the power of Judicial Review.

The judiciary is the system of courts that interprets and guards the Indian Constitution. With reference to the Supreme Court of India, answer the following: What is meant by the term Original Jurisdiction? Mention any three cases which come under this jurisdiction.
Mention any three changes made in the administration with the end of the Company’s Rule.
State any three policies promised to Indians in Queen Victoria’s Proclamation.
Mention any four changes made in the army after the Revolt.
Who partitioned Bengal? Mention any two points to explain the perspective of the Nationalists regarding the actual motive behind the decision of Partition.
What was the objective of the Assertive Nationalists? Mention any two contributions of Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
In which year was the Muslim League formed? Mention any three objectives of the Muslim League.

(i) Name the Viceroy who announced the plan for smooth transfer of power. Mention any two clauses of his plan with reference to the Princely States. [3]
(ii) Mention any three reasons for the acceptance of his plan by the Congress. [3]
(iii) Mention any four provisions of the Indian Independence Act of 1947. [4]

questions.text:
The final act of the long-drawn-out negotiations took place at Versailles on Saturday afternoon, and to-day Germany and the Allies – always with the exception of America – are at peace. Peace is a blessed word, and both the word and the fact are welcome to-day. So far as Germany is concerned there is for the present an end of strife, and at least a formal return to the decent relations of civilised states.
Editorial: Peace in force (12 January 1920)
The Guardian
Mention any three causes of the World War which ended with the signing of the treaty being discussed in the passage above.
extractionIssues: The printed passage (shared by Question 9 (i)-(iii)) is repeated in each sub-part.
